title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The cache now knows the text
summary: Reopening a file after it changed outside the editor could show the previous version folds, colours and lenses. The five caches are keyed on the content itself now.

highlights.title: A reopened file shows itself
highlights.description: Closing a document destroys it, and reopening builds a new one whose version restarts at 1. Two different texts of the same size at the same path answered as one. Reproduced with two files of exactly 64 characters: the second was given the first one fold ranges.

highlights.title: Identity is the text, not its size
highlights.description: Folding, semantic tokens, the sealed when lens, the state provenance lens and the shared symbol analysis all key on a content fingerprint now.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The fingerprint takes 4.7 microseconds on the average file of a real project of 3187 Kotlin files, and 0.095 ms on the largest, against 1.7 ms to recompute one file folds.
The repository benchmark shows no measurable change.
